title: 2026-10-22_Pulse_Secure_RADIALPULSE_Trojan_Investigation_82f
description: Investigate the compromised victim host to identify and contain the RADIALPULSE trojan.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has been compromised by the RADIALPULSE trojan, which targets Pulse Secure VPN devices. This malware bypasses authentication, persists across upgrades, and maintains access through webshells. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malware's persistence mechanisms, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system. Enumerate running services and distinguish legitimate services from trojan-related services.
levels.solution: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or out of place. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. The suspicious service related to the trojan is the `network-diagnostics` service. The final flag is `network-diagnostics.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or out of place.

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Task or Timer
levels.content: Determine whether a scheduled task or timer is responsible for automatically executing the malware. Identify scheduled execution persistence mechanisms (e.g., cron, systemd timers, Windows Scheduled Tasks).
levels.solution: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any that might be related to the malware. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. The scheduled task or timer responsible for executing the malware is the `network-diagnostics.timer` service. The final flag is `network-diagnostics.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd timers and services to find any that might be related to the malware.

levels.title: Locate Malware Files
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the compromised host. Correlate suspicious activity with files introduced by the trojan.
levels.solution: Search for hidden directories and files that might contain malware components or collected data. Use the command `find / -name '.netd' 2>/dev/null` to search for the malware files. The files installed by the malware are located in `/usr/local/lib/.netd` and `/var/lib/.netd`. The final flag is `/usr/local/lib/.netd|/var/lib/.netd`.

hints.content: Search for hidden directories and files that might contain malware components or collected data.
